description: Tier-1 safety-critical activities. Each requires a named human sign-off and BLOCKS P6 export until signed (CLAUDE.md rule 5, DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 7). Tier-1 rules are HSE-owned; changing them requires an HSE-role sign-off in admin (ADMIN_SPEC.md section 5).
provenance_summary: The five Tier-1 activities and their stated reasons are transcribed from DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 7. The permit_predecessors and hold_point wording are the model's elaboration and are NOT from that table - an HSE lead must review them before they gate a real plan.

entries.why: Arc flash and electrocution risk; requires lock-out/tag-out discipline.

entries.activity_pattern: Work in or next to live data halls (brownfield)
entries.why: Concurrent operations beside energised IT load.

provenance.note: Activity and reason from DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 7 row 5. permit_predecessors and hold_points are MODEL-ELABORATED and need HSE review. applies_when_site_context ADDED FOR REVIEW: the pattern already says "(brownfield)" in prose, but prose is not a condition the engine can read, so this rule fired on greenfield projects too. Found when the fit-out fragnet was added: "Raised floor and plinth installation to data halls" shares the words "data" and "halls" with this pattern, which was enough for the two-word keyword match, and a routine raised-floor activity on a greenfield site was marked Tier-1 and BLOCKED EXPORT. Wrongly blocking export is not a safe failure: it teaches a planner that the block is noise.
